football_evidence.question: Can Texas State contain Oregon State’s explosive runs?
football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward Texas State, and its own breakdown accounts for about 0.0 of the 4.0 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.
supporting: When Texas State has the ball (the run game against the run defense): Texas State’s offense averages 6.1 yards per carry, and Oregon State’s defense allows 5.0 yards per carry (FBS average 5.0).

When Texas State has the ball (third down): Texas State’s offense converts 52.8% of its third downs, and Oregon State’s defense allows opponents to convert 37.3% of their third downs (FBS average 39.6%).

When Texas State has the ball (big plays on the ground): Texas State’s offense turns 8.6% of its runs into explosive gains, and Oregon State’s defense gives up explosive gains on 6.6% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).

When Texas State has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Texas State’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 13.7% of its runs, and Oregon State’s defense stops 14.6% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.5%).
contradicting: When Oregon State has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Oregon State’s offense has allowed a sack on 3.9% of its dropbacks, and Texas State’s defense sacks the quarterback on 3.2% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).

When Oregon State has the ball (early downs): Oregon State’s offense succeeds on 52.6% of its first- and second-down plays, and Texas State’s defense allows success on 43.4% of first- and second-down plays (FBS average 42.5%).

When Oregon State has the ball (the red zone): Oregon State’s offense succeeds on 60.4% of its red-zone plays, and Texas State’s defense allows success on 44.7% of opponent red-zone plays (FBS average 43.5%).

When Oregon State has the ball (down-to-down efficiency): Oregon State’s offense succeeds on 52.0% of its offensive plays, and Texas State’s defense allows opponents to succeed on 42.4% of their plays (FBS average 42.3%).
quarterbacks: Braden Atkinson has completed 223 of 333 passes (67.0%) for 3,017 yards, 9.1 yards per attempt, 27 touchdowns and 2 interceptions in eight games for Oregon State, and has been sacked on 14 of 347 dropbacks.

Brad Jackson has completed 156 of 233 passes (67.0%) for 1,933 yards, 8.3 yards per attempt, 18 touchdowns and 4 interceptions in eight games for Texas State, and has been sacked on 9 of 242 dropbacks.
